full_judgment:
4. On 6-5-85/7-5-85 a petition on behalf of the accused-petitioners was moved for releasing them under section 339C(4) CrPC. On 8-5-85 after hearing both the sides the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate rejected the petitions and framed charges under section 467/408/109 of the Penal Cole. Being aggrieved by the said order dated 8-5-85 of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate fixing 2-6-85 beyond the period of 90 working days counting limitation from 9-2-85 the prosecution moved the Sessions Judge, Chittagong u/s 5268 CrPC, being Criminal Motion Nos. 333/85, 334/85, 335/85, 336/85 and 330/8S for transferring the split up 5 cases to another competent court. The learned Sessions Judge by his judgment and order dated 31-8-85 transferred the cases to Mr MA Muktadir, Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong for disposal. Mr MA Muktadir, Metropolitan Magistrate in the order sheet observed that he has got no power to try a case under section 467 of the Penal Code and with such remark he sent the case back to Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate thereafter sent the case record back to the Sessions Judge for necessary order; the learned Sessions Judge transferred the case to the court of Mr MA Salam, Additional District Magistrate for disposal. The Additional District Magistrate Chittagong received the said 5 cases on 17-12-85 and after reading over the charges to the accused-petitioners fixed all the cases on 4-1-86 for evidence, The learned Advocate for the accused-petitioners informs this Court that the accused petitioners are being tried by the Additional District Magistrate and the evidence is being recorded It may further be stated that the two accused-petitioners had already moved the Sessions Judge, Chittagong under section 439A CrPC. being Criminal Motion No. 462/85 on the grounds that after the first charge sheet was received by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate on 29-12-83 and after taking cognizance of the case on that very date the case was received by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate by transfer to his own file 29-1-84 that the statutory period of limitation as provided in Section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure had expired after 60 working days from 29-1-84, that the further proceedings in respect of the trial ought to have been stopped and the accused-persons on the expiry of the statutory period of limitation ought to have been released under sub-section (4) of section 339C of the Code Criminal of Procedure, that there is no provision in law for the investigating Officer to split up the charge-sheet, that the statutory period of limitation of 60 working days having expired even from the date of receipt of the 5 cases along with the 5 split up charge-sheets on 9-2-85 by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate functioning as trial court the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate ought to have stopped further proceedings and ought to have released the accused-persons under sub-section (4) of section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure since between 9-2-85 to 27-5-85 eighty-six (86) working days had expired and that the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate had not extended the period of limitation of 30 days for another 30 days under sub-section (3) of the said section by recording reasons in writing. 

 "The period of limitation as provided under section 339C of CrPC. will commerce from the date of receipt of the record by the Magistrate for trial. This means the record should be sent to the trial Court after observing all formalities hut here in the present case wrong charge-sheet was submitted and the learned trial court had to send it back for rectification and the period under wrong charge-sheet cannot be counted in the disposal of the case. This section (339C of CrPC) clearly indicates that the trial court should receive the complete case record for' trial without any defect so that the same may be disposed of within the statutory period of limitation Here in the present case the record was received by the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate for trial on 29-1-84 and then on 7-6-84 the prosecution tiled a petition stating that the 10 submitted one charge, sheet for 5 distinct offences. These offences were committed from the year 1979-1983 and the prosecution prayed for directing the 10 for submit- ting split up charge-sheet as these offences committed from 1979-1983 cannot be tried together. Section 233 CrPC provided that for every distinct offence of which any person is accused there shall be a separate charge, and every such charge shall be tried separately except in the cases mentioned in sections 234, 235, 236 and 239 All these indicate that previous charge-sheet was not legally submitted and as there was no legally submitted charge-sheet, it cannot be found that the case was fully ready for trial though as a matter of fact the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate received the case for trial". 

 5. Regarding the second point raised before us by the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioners in respect of counting additional 30 working days without expressly extending the period of limitation In writing with reasons the learned Sessions Judge observed in the said judgment dated 31-8-85 in Criminal Motion. No. 462/85 as follows: 

 9. The investigating officer in the present case submitted charge-sheet for criminal breach of trust and dishonest misappropriation by the two accused-petitioners for the period of 5 years from 1979 1983. The said charge-sheet is, therefore, defective and erroneous and since it is in contravention of section 233 read with sections 222 (2) and 234 CrPC, such charge sheet is no charge-sheet in the eye of law. Therefore, the acceptance of the charge-sheet and receipt of the case by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate as a trial Court on 29-1-84 will not mean that the limitation provided in section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall start running from 29-1-84 (excluding the Government holidays). 

 10. Since the charge sheet submitted was not in accordance with law, the case cannot be treated as ready for trial and therefore, inspite of the receipt of the case by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate as a trial court the limitation provided in 339C CrPC will not begin to run. 

 12. In view of the expression "conclude the trial of a case within sixty days from the date of which the case is received by him for trial" in section 339C (1) CrPC the date of taking cognizance has no significance for counting the period of limitation. The period of limitation is to be counted from the date of receipt of the case by the trial court concerned. So far as the question of split up charge sheet is concerned, it may be stated that we have already quoted the order passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate on 7-6-84. The said order is to the effect that the prosecution has filed a petition for submitting split up charge sheet (as it is defective), that the learned Magistrate kept the petition in the record and transferred the case to his general file (as the case was not ready).
